hotel.name: Rainbow Palace Yoyogi
hotel.station: Minami-Shinjuku (Odakyu Line) ~8 min walk · Yoyogi (JR / Toei Oedo) ~12 min walk

arrival.title: Arrival: Narita Airport → Rainbow Palace Yoyogi
arrival.summary: Land, get through immigration and customs, sort out cash, phone data and IC cards, then ride the Narita Express to Shinjuku and one more stop to the hotel. Keep the evening easy – dinner near the hotel and an early night so Day 1 can start at 9:00.
arrival.duration: About 2–3 hours from landing to the hotel door (immigration + baggage 45–90 min, train ~80–90 min, transfer and walk ~20 min).

airportSteps.title: Before landing (on the plane)
airportSteps.detail: Open Visit Japan Web screenshots: one immigration + customs QR code per person (finish registration at least 6 hours before landing, before you fly). Keep the three passports and a pen in one easy pocket. Use the plane toilet before landing – immigration queues can be long.

airportSteps.title: 1 · Walk to Immigration
airportSteps.detail: Follow the yellow 'Arrival / Immigration' signs. Join the 'Foreign Passport' (non-Japanese) lane together – families stay together at one booth.

airportSteps.title: 2 · Immigration booth
airportSteps.detail: Show passports and your Visit Japan Web immigration QR (or a paper landing card if you didn't register). You (16+) give fingerprints and a photo; children under 16 don't. The officer puts a 'Temporary Visitor' landing sticker in each passport – check all three have one.

airportSteps.title: 3 · Baggage claim
airportSteps.detail: Find your flight on the screens for the carousel number. Trolleys are free. Count the bags before leaving.

airportSteps.title: 4 · Customs
airportSteps.detail: Use the customs e-gates with your Visit Japan Web customs QR + passport (or hand in the paper customs form – one per family). Most families have nothing to declare. Medicines must be within the limits (see Prepare tab).

airportSteps.title: 5 · Arrivals hall: cash
airportSteps.detail: Withdraw ¥30,000–50,000 from a 7-Eleven (Seven Bank) or Japan Post ATM – they accept foreign cards. Many small shops, food stalls and temples are cash only.

airportSteps.title: 6 · Phone data
airportSteps.detail: Activate your eSIM (bought before the trip) or pick up a pocket Wi-Fi at its counter. Check Google Maps works before leaving the airport.

airportSteps.title: 7 · IC cards (Suica)
airportSteps.detail: Go to the JR East Travel Service Center at the airport station (B1). Welcome Suica (tourist card, no deposit, valid 28 days) is sold there and at machines. You: adult card. 12-year-old: buy an ADULT card – from April 1 they pay adult fares. 10-year-old: CHILD Welcome Suica at the counter (bring the child's passport). Load ~¥2,000–3,000 each. iPhone users can also use the Welcome Suica Mobile app.

airportSteps.title: 8 · Train tickets
airportSteps.detail: At the same JR East Travel Service Center buy Narita Express (N'EX) tickets to Shinjuku. Foreign passport holders can buy the N'EX round-trip ticket (adult ¥5,200, valid 14 days) if you will fly home from Narita; otherwise one-way (~¥3,070–3,330 adult, children about half). On March 31 BOTH kids still count as children (school year ends March 31). All N'EX seats are reserved – ask for three seats together and write down the car number.

airportSteps.title: 9 · Optional: send big suitcases to the hotel
airportSteps.detail: Luggage-delivery counters (e.g. Yamato / ABC) in the arrivals hall can send suitcases to the hotel, usually arriving the next day. Keep an overnight bag with pyjamas, chargers and medicines. Ask the hotel first whether they accept deliveries. Price per bag – check at the counter.

airportSteps.title: 10 · Last stop before the train
airportSteps.detail: Toilets, water and a konbini snack for the ride. Then follow the red 'JR Lines' signs down to the platform.

routes.name: Recommended: Narita Express (N'EX) + Odakyu Line
routes.cost: ≈ ¥3,100–3,300 adult + about half per child (one-way) · or N'EX round trip ¥5,200 adult
routes.why: Reserved seats, big luggage racks, no changes until Shinjuku. Easiest with kids after a long flight.
steps: Take the N'EX bound for Shinjuku from the B1 platform (trains roughly every 30–60 min – check the board).
IMPORTANT: N'EX trains split at Tokyo station. Sit in the car number printed on your ticket – that's the part going to Shinjuku.
Put big suitcases in the racks at the end of the car (they have a lock). Ride ~80–90 min.
Get off at Shinjuku. Follow signs to the 'Odakyu Line' (west side of the station). Tap in with Suica.
Take an Odakyu LOCAL train (各駅停車, 'Local') one stop to Minami-Shinjuku (~2 min). Expresses don't stop there.
From Minami-Shinjuku walk ~8 min to Rainbow Palace Yoyogi (3-55-1 Yoyogi). Open the hotel in Google Maps before you leave the platform.
Alternative last step: JR Chuo-Sobu local one stop to Yoyogi, then ~12 min walk. With very heavy bags, a taxi from Shinjuku South Exit is the only taxi this trip should need.

routes.name: Easiest with sleepy kids: Airport Limousine Bus to Shinjuku
routes.cost: ≈ ¥3,200–3,900 adult, children half – check current fare
routes.why: Staff load your suitcases; no stairs or changes. Slower in traffic.
steps: Buy tickets at the Airport Limousine counter in the arrivals hall (or online).
Go to the bus stop number on your ticket; staff put suitcases in the hold – keep the baggage tags.
Get off at Busta Shinjuku (Shinjuku Expressway Bus Terminal, 4F above the South Exit).
From Busta Shinjuku walk ~15 min to the hotel, or go down to the Odakyu Line and ride one stop to Minami-Shinjuku.

routes.name: Budget/fastest train: Keisei Skyliner + JR Yamanote
routes.cost: Skyliner reserved seat + JR fare – check current prices
routes.why: Fast to Nippori, but one change with luggage on stairs/escalators.
steps: Buy Skyliner tickets at the Keisei counter (B1).
Change to the JR Yamanote Line (green) toward Ikebukuro/Shinjuku – ~20 min to Shinjuku, or ride on to Yoyogi.
Continue as in the recommended route (Odakyu to Minami-Shinjuku, or walk from Yoyogi).

items.text: Passports for all three, valid for the whole trip (check the kids' expiry dates)
Check visa-free entry for your nationality. JESTA (Japan's future e-travel authorization) is NOT needed for 2027 trips – ignore sites selling it
Register on Visit Japan Web (one account can hold the whole family) and complete immigration + customs at least 6 hours before landing; screenshot each person's QR code
Travelling as the only parent? Carry a consent letter from the other parent if your home country or airline may ask
Travel insurance with medical cover for all three (save the emergency number)
Hotel booking confirmation + address in Japanese and English (東京都渋谷区代々木3-55-1) – printed and on the phone
Flight times, terminal and booking codes saved offline
Photos of passports and insurance stored in the cloud and printed
Ikebukuro Bosaikan earthquake simulator for Mon Apr 5 – bookings open up to 5 months ahead (≈ from early November 2026)
TOKYO SKYTREE weekday advance tickets for Fri Apr 2 (cheaper online)
Kirby Café Tokyo for Fri Apr 2 – reservations sell out quickly
Tokyo Joypolis e-tickets for Sun Apr 4 (if you choose it)
SHIBUYA SKY for Thu Apr 1 (optional – the free Hikarie view is the budget alternative)
Decide N'EX round trip (¥5,200 adult, foreign passport) vs one-way – depends on your return airport
LEGOLAND Discovery Center Tokyo dated ticket (optional)
Two payment cards without foreign-transaction fees; tell your bank you're travelling
Plan to withdraw ¥30,000–50,000 at Narita (7-Eleven / Japan Post ATMs take foreign cards)
Coin purse for ¥100 coins (gashapon, lockers, crane games)
Kids' souvenir and arcade budgets agreed before the trip
Tax-free shopping changes to a refund system from November 2026 – keep receipts and passports when shopping
eSIM or pocket Wi-Fi for at least two devices (so a kid's phone or tablet can call you)
Apps: Google Maps (download Tokyo offline), Google Translate (Japanese offline + camera), Welcome Suica Mobile (iPhone), Visit Japan Web, this app installed on the home screen
Plug adapter for Japan's Type A sockets (two flat pins, 100 V – most phone chargers are fine)
Power bank in hand luggage (not in checked bags) + cables for everyone
Kids' headphones for the flight and trains
Medicines in original packaging with a copy of the prescription; prescription meds up to 1 month, non-prescription up to 2 months (more needs a Yakkan Shoumei import certificate)
Do NOT pack pseudoephedrine products (e.g. Sudafed, Actifed, Vicks inhaler) or Adderall-type stimulants – they are prohibited in Japan
Kids' fever/pain medicine, plasters, motion-sickness tablets, any allergy medicine (spring = cedar-pollen season)
Hand sanitizer, tissues, wet wipes
Emergency numbers saved: police 110, ambulance/fire 119, Japan Visitor Hotline 050-3816-2787

preparation.title: Clothes (Tokyo early April: mild days, cool evenings)

items.text: Layers: T-shirts, a warm sweater/fleece and a light jacket for each person
Compact umbrella or light rain jackets
Comfortable walking shoes that slip on and off easily (shoes come off in some places)
Good socks without holes – everyone will see them when shoes come off
Small hand towels – many public toilets have no paper towels
Overnight bag packed separately (in case suitcases are sent ahead from the airport)
Refillable water bottles
Small bag for rubbish (public bins are rare)
Snacks for queues
Picnic sheet for sakura days (Shinjuku Gyoen, Sumida Park)
Contact card for each child: your phone number, hotel name and address in Japanese + English

preparation.title: Talk with the kids before the trip

items.text: 'If we get separated' rule: stay where you are, or ask station staff and show your contact card
Quiet on trains, no eating while walking, stand on the left on escalators, shoes off when you see slippers
Arcade rule: under-16s leave arcades by 18:00
Five phrases: konnichiwa, arigatō, sumimasen, onegai shimasu, toire wa doko desu ka?
Online check-in, seats together for all three
Bag weight checked; leave space for souvenirs
House keys, lights, plants/pets arranged
Charge every device the night before

days.title: Sakura gardens, fire engines & Godzilla
days.summary: Start the trip next to the hotel with Shinjuku Gyoen's cherry blossoms, a free fire-engine museum and Godzilla peering over Shinjuku. Afternoon in Harajuku and Shibuya for gyoza, anime treasures, arcades and a free (or paid) skyline view.
days.budget: 7-stop route ≈ ¥10,100 for all three (adult ¥4,100 · age 12 ¥3,400 · age 10 ¥2,600). Attractions ¥500, food ¥8,100 (budget meals), transport ¥1,500 (IC card; the 12-year-old pays adult fares from Apr 1). Extras (arcades, gashapon, souvenirs) not included.
before: Shinjuku Gyoen is in peak sakura week: arrive at 9:00; no alcohol, bags checked.
Arcades: under-16s must leave by 18:00 – do them in the afternoon.
SHIBUYA SKY is optional and expensive – book online only if you want it.

days.title: Skytree, penguins & old Edo
days.summary: A Friday in east Tokyo: the reopened Edo-Tokyo Museum, then Skytree, Kirby and Pokémon under one roof and penguins at Sumida Aquarium. Finish with riverside cherry blossoms and arcade games.
days.budget: 7-stop route ≈ ¥27,250 for all three (adult ¥11,600 · age 12 ¥8,700 · age 10 ¥6,950). Attractions ¥16,650, food ¥8,100 (budget meals), transport ¥2,500 (IC card; the 12-year-old pays adult fares from Apr 1). Extras (arcades, gashapon, souvenirs) not included.
before: Book Skytree (weekday advance) and Kirby Café online.
The Sumo Museum is weekdays only – today is your chance.
Sumida Park sakura: Friday is calmer than the weekend.

days.title: Rides, baseball & retro games
days.summary: Saturday of rides at Tokyo Dome City, Ohtani at the Baseball Museum and an Edo garden in bloom. Then Kanda's anime shrine, trains rushing past at mAAch ecute and retro arcade games in Akihabara.
days.budget: 7-stop route ≈ ¥20,400 for all three (adult ¥7,700 · age 12 ¥7,300 · age 10 ¥5,400). Attractions ¥10,300, food ¥8,100 (budget meals), transport ¥2,000 (IC card; the 12-year-old pays adult fares from Apr 1). Extras (arcades, gashapon, souvenirs) not included.
before: Saturday + spring break: ride queues grow after 11:00 – start at Tokyo Dome City at opening.
Check the ride passport price calendar the day before.
Origami Kaikan is usually closed Sundays – Saturday works.

days.title: Bay day: footbaths, Gundam & Joypolis
days.summary: Sunday by the bay: market brunch and a free footbath at Toyosu, an earthquake-survival adventure at Sona Area and Gundam at DiverCity. End with arcades, Joypolis (or LEGOLAND) and takoyaki with retro sweets at DECKS.
days.budget: 7-stop route ≈ ¥30,150 for all three (adult ¥11,500 · age 12 ¥10,000 · age 10 ¥8,650). Attractions ¥17,800, food ¥8,100 (budget meals), transport ¥4,250 (IC card; the 12-year-old pays adult fares from Apr 1). Extras (arcades, gashapon, souvenirs) not included.
before: Toyosu Market is CLOSED on Sundays – Senkyaku Banrai (food hall) is open.
Miraikan is closed until Apr 23, 2027 and the giant Gundam statue is gone (2026).
Joypolis is expensive (~¥16,000 for three) – decide in advance; Round1 is the cheap alternative.
Yurikamome/Rinkai trains are not covered by the Tokyo Subway Ticket.
Optional evening: walk the free Rainbow Bridge promenade (~1.7 km; closed 3rd Monday and in strong wind) – eat first, there is no food on the bridge.

days.title: Pokémon, capsule toys & the rooftop aquarium
days.summary: Monday-proof day (many museums close on Mondays, Sunshine City doesn't): earthquake simulator, rooftop aquarium and a planetarium. Then Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo, 3,000 capsule-toy machines, Namja Town's gyoza and a sunset 240 m up.
days.budget: 7-stop route ≈ ¥25,650 for all three (adult ¥9,600 · age 12 ¥9,200 · age 10 ¥6,850). Attractions ¥16,300, food ¥8,100 (budget meals), transport ¥1,250 (IC card; the 12-year-old pays adult fares from Apr 1). Extras (arcades, gashapon, souvenirs) not included.
before: Monday April 5: most city museums are closed – this day avoids them.
Book the Bosaikan (earthquake simulator) in advance; tours are in Japanese.
Bring ¥100 coins for Gashapon (change machines inside).
